title: Stage 5: Indexes and the dashboard
summary: Index the fact table for the queries the dashboard runs, prove it with the plan, and write the final dashboard queries.

steps.title: Tuning for the dashboard
body: The dashboard runs three kinds of queries against `fact_sales`:
1. date ranges grouped by channel (the monthly view)
Today the table has 13 rows; in five years it'll have millions. Index for the access paths you know about, and check the plan rather than hoping:
- The monthly report filters and groups by date, then reads channel and revenue: a **covering** index `(order_date, channel, revenue_cents)`.
- Customer pages search by `customer_id`, a foreign key, which SQLite doesn't index for you.

CREATE TABLE stg_orders ( order_ref TEXT NOT NULL, order_date TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL, customer_name TEXT NOT NULL, isbn TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, qty INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (qty > 0), unit_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (unit_cents >= 0), channel TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (channel IN ('web', 'shop')), PRIMARY KEY (order_ref, isbn) );

INSERT OR IGNORE INTO stg_orders (order_ref, order_date, email, customer_name, isbn, title, qty, unit_cents, channel) SELECT trim(order_ref), CASE WHEN order_date LIKE '__/__/____' THEN substr(order_date, 7, 4) || '-' || substr(order_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(order_date, 1, 2) ELSE order_date END, lower(trim(customer_email)), trim(customer_name), trim(isbn), trim(title), CAST(trim(qty) AS INTEGER), CAST(ROUND(CAST(replace(trim(unit_price), '£', '') AS REAL) * 100) AS INTEGER), lower(trim(channel)) FROM raw_orders;
CREATE TABLE dim_customer (customer_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, name TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE dim_book (book_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, isbn TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, title TEXT NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO dim_customer (email, name) SELECT DISTINCT email, customer_name FROM stg_orders;
INSERT INTO dim_book (isbn, title) SELECT DISTINCT isbn, title FROM stg_orders;

CREATE TABLE fact_sales ( order_ref TEXT NOT NULL, order_date TEXT NOT NULL, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_customer(customer_id), book_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_book(book_id), channel TEXT NOT NULL, qty INTEGER NOT NULL, revenue_cents INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (order_ref, book_id) );

INSERT INTO fact_sales SELECT s.order_ref, s.order_date, c.customer_id, b.book_id, s.channel, s.qty, s.qty * s.unit_cents FROM stg_orders AS s JOIN dim_customer AS c ON c.email = s.email JOIN dim_book AS b ON b.isbn = s.isbn;

CREATE VIEW v_monthly_revenue AS SELECT substr(order_date, 1, 7) AS month, channel, COUNT(DISTINCT order_ref) AS orders, SUM(qty) AS books, SUM(revenue_cents) AS revenue_cents FROM fact_sales GROUP BY month, channel;

CREATE VIEW v_customer_value AS SELECT c.name, c.email, COUNT(DISTINCT f.order_ref) AS orders, SUM(f.revenue_cents) AS revenue_cents, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(f.revenue_cents) DESC) AS value_rank FROM fact_sales AS f JOIN dim_customer AS c ON c.customer_id = f.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name, c.email;

steps.title: Dashboard: revenue to date
prompt: The headline chart: for each **month**, return **revenue_cents** (both channels) and **to_date** (the running total), in month order. Use `v_monthly_revenue`.

Tables: `dim_customer(customer_id, email, name)`, `dim_book(book_id, isbn, title)`, `fact_sales(order_ref, order_date, customer_id, book_id, channel, qty, revenue_cents)`, views `v_monthly_revenue` and `v_customer_value`.
solution: SUM(SUM(revenue_cents)) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS to_date

steps.title: Dashboard: best seller per channel
prompt: The last tile: the **best-selling book in each channel** by copies. Return **channel**, **title** and **copies**. If two books tie for first in a channel, show both.
Tables: `dim_customer(customer_id, email, name)`, `dim_book(book_id, isbn, title)`, `fact_sales(order_ref, order_date, customer_id, book_id, channel, qty, revenue_cents)`.
solution: SELECT f.channel, b.title, SUM(f.qty) AS copies,
RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY f.channel ORDER BY SUM(f.qty) DESC) AS r
JOIN dim_book AS b ON b.book_id = f.book_id
SELECT channel, title, copies FROM per_book WHERE r = 1;
